title: Label-driven subnet swap and conditional endpoint sticky-routing for control plane
author: Priya Sharma
release_notes: Introduce label-driven subnet swap to allow staged control-plane subnet rotation with sticky endpoint routing and conditional DNS TTL migration. Backwards compatible; rollout controlled via installer flags.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers running private control planes in multi-AZ deployments asked for a safer, auditable path to rotate control-plane subnets and move PrivateLink/ENI endpoints with minimal per-request disruption. Existing approaches either required full cutovers (causing short traffic spikes) or manual operator steps that were error-prone. This change implements a label-driven subnet swap flow plus a conditional endpoint sticky-routing mechanism that keeps active control-plane connections pinned to existing endpoints while new allocations warm up, and only shifts DNS TTLs after healthy probes pass.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a label-based subnet claim mechanism in the Terraform modules: controlplane_subnet.claim_label and controlplane_subnet.swap_marker. Allows the installer to mark a new subnet as candidate and then flip ownership with a controlled window.
- Implements an endpoint sticky-router sidecar in the private controlplane Helm chart (kube-controller extension) that pins in-flight client sessions to the existing PrivateLink/ENI endpoint during rollout, falling back to the new endpoint only after graceful drain.
- Introduces a DNS migration helper: a small orchestration job (helm hook + installer runner) that performs health probes, reduces DNS TTL, and atomically updates Route53/Cloud DNS records only when probes succeed. Supports conditional TTL rollback on probe failures.
- Exposes installer flags for staged rollouts: --staged-subnet-swap, --endpoint-sticky-duration, --dns-conditional-migrate. These default to safe conservative values.
- Adds end-to-end acceptance tests and a canary job in CI that simulates a swap (with mocked ENI endpoints) to validate orchestration and failure recovery paths.

Design notes and constraints:
- The label-driven swap keeps resource names stable (no recreation of core control-plane instances) so customers with strict IP allowlists or external firewall mappings experience minimal churn.
- Sticky routing intentionally pins high-latency/long-lived requests to the old endpoint for up to endpoint-sticky-duration to avoid mid-request failures; short requests are routed according to policy to maximize cutover speed.
- DNS migration lowering TTL is best-effort; in some cross-account setups the authoritative DNS changes may be delayed. The job logs detailed diffs and writes a rollback marker if the migration does not meet the configured health thresholds within the timeout.

- [x] Terraform module: controlplane_subnet claims and swap_marker support

Review conversation (highlights):
- Diego Alvarez (review): "This looks promising. Two safety asks: 1) can we gate the default behavior behind an explicit feature flag in releases, and 2) ensure IAM for the DNS migrator is least-privilege and auditable?"
- Author reply: "Added installer flags (disabled by default) and tightened IAM policy to only put-get-change records on the target hosted zone; also added CloudTrail note in docs."
- Mei Lin (review): "The sticky-router sidecar needs resource limits and health endpoints so kube can kill/restart it safely."
- Author reply: "Added resource requests/limits and a /healthz probe; updated Helm values to tune them."
- Omar Haddad (approval): "Verified test harness can simulate partial failures; LGTM after minor nits fixed."

CI and testing:
- Unit tests: pass (go and TF validation checks)
- Integration canary: ran in CI with a mocked ENI endpoint cluster; highlighted one race where swap_marker wasn't set before DNS change — fixed by introducing a barrier step in swap.go
- Lint: terraform fmt/tflint, go vet, helm lint — all pass on final run

Rollout and migration instructions (for release / ops):
1) Enable feature with installer flag --staged-subnet-swap=true in a single region.
2) Provision candidate subnet (installer will label it with claim_label).
3) Wait for health checks and warm-up period.
4) Trigger swap controller (installer exposes a staged-swap subcommand).
5) Endpoint sticky-router will keep in-flight sessions bound; DNS migrator will lower TTL and run probes.
6) On successful probes, DNS migrator updates records and writes swap_marker to confirm completion.
7) If probes fail, migrator increases TTL back and the swap is aborted with rollback marker written; operator may investigate logs and retry.

Known limitations and future work:
- Cross-account DNS where RecordSet changes are proxied require separate delegation hooks; we added a TODO to support delegated-write flows.
- Multi-region simultaneous swaps are not supported in this PR; follow-up will add a global orchestration coordinator.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from reviewers. Changelog and release notes have been updated.
